Rashi on Gittin 25a:10:1.english: Well [understood] - Because of this, he acquires [portions for] his brothers together with him:

Rashi on Gittin 25a:10:2.english: People may be registered - [Referring to] one who wishes to be registered:

Rashi on Gittin 25a:10:3.hebrew: ומושכין את ידיהן - מי שהיה נמנה ורוצה לימשך ולהמנות על אחר, מושך ידיו הימנו:
Rashi on Gittin 25a:10:3.english: And they withdraw their hands - One who was registered [for one Paschal offering] and wishes to withdraw and be registered for another [offering] withdraws his hands from it:

Rashi on Gittin 25a:10:4.hebrew: עד שישחט - אבל לאחר שחיטה, לא נמנין ולא נמשכין, דכתיב: "ואם ימעט הבית" — אם באו להמעט ולהמשך ממנו, "מהיות משה" — בחיותו של שה יתמעטו:
Rashi on Gittin 25a:10:4.english: Until it is slaughtered - But after slaughter, [people] may neither be registered nor withdraw, as it is written: "And if the household be too small" — [that is,] if they come to diminish [their number] and withdraw from it, "from being [for] a lamb" [homiletically reading *miheyot* ("from being") as *be-chayuto* ("while alive")] — while the lamb is alive they must diminish [their number]:

Rashi on Gittin 25a:11:1.hebrew: תניא נמי הכי - דלא נתכוין אלא לזרזן, ומיהו כולהו אמנינהו:
Rashi on Gittin 25a:11:1.english: It is also taught thus - that he intended only to spur them on, yet he registered all of them [for the Paschal offering]:

Rashi on Gittin 25a:11:2.hebrew: ובנים שפלים - ולא קתני "ונמצאו בנות זוכות בפסח, ובנים לא זכו":
Rashi on Gittin 25a:11:2.english: And the sons [were] lazy - and it does not state, "and the daughters were found to merit [a share in] the Paschal offering, and the sons did not merit [it]":

Rashi on Gittin 25a:12:1.hebrew: אמר אביי קבעי מיניה - אתמוהי מתמה אביי ברב יהודה ורב אושעיא: קבעי מיניה "לאיזו שתצא בפתח תחילה", דתלה (זה) המתנה בדעת אחרים, וקפשיט ליה "לאיזו שארצה", דהיינו תולה בדעת עצמו! דילמא תולה בדעת עצמו לית לן ברירה, דמדאתני ברישא, גילה בדעתו שהיה פוסח על שתי סעיפים, וליכא למימר הוברר דמעיקרא דעתיה להאי; אבל זה שתלה באחרים, גמר בדעתיה מעיקרא לאיזו שתצא:
Rashi on Gittin 25a:12:1.english: Abaye said: He asks him - Abaye is expressing astonishment at Rav Yehudah and Rav Oshaya: [Rav Oshaya] asks him about "[the bill of divorce is for] whichever [wife] exits the entrance first," where this stipulator made [the matter] dependent on the decision of others, and [Rav Yehudah] resolves it for him from "[for] whichever I will want," which is making [it] dependent on his own decision! Perhaps [where one] makes [it] dependent on his own decision, we do not hold of bereirah [retroactive clarification], because since he stipulated at the outset [that he would decide later], he revealed his mind that he was wavering between two options, and one cannot say that it became clarified that from the beginning his mind was on this one; whereas this one who made [it] dependent on others resolved in his mind from the beginning [to divorce] whichever one exits [first]:

Rashi on Gittin 25a:15:1.hebrew: מבין הכותים - קודם גזירה, ואין לו כלי להפריש תרומות ומעשרות בהן, והוא צריך לשתות. וכותים גירי אמת חשיב להו, ואין ארץ ישראל נפקעת מקדושתה על ידיהם, והן חשודין על המעשרות ועל התרומה; ולא כעמי הארץ, שרובן מעשרין וכולן מפרישין תרומה, אבל כותים חשודין על הכל, והלוקח מהן צריך לעשר ודאי:
Rashi on Gittin 25a:15:1.english: From among the Cutheans - [This was] before the decree [forbidding their wine], and he has no vessel into which to separate terumot and tithes, and he needs to drink. Now, [the Tanna] considers Cutheans to be true converts, so the Land of Israel is not divested of its sanctity through them, and they are suspected [of neglecting] tithes and terumah; and [they are] not like amei ha'aretz [unlearned Jews], most of whom tithe and all of whom separate terumah, whereas Cutheans are suspected regarding everything, and one who purchases from them must tithe [it as] definitely untithed [produce]:

Rashi on Gittin 25a:1:1.hebrew: קטן ואנפיליא - קילצו"ן של בגד; לאו חליצה כלל, ד"איש" ו"נעל" כתובים בפרשה: "ואם לא יחפוץ האיש" וגו':
Rashi on Gittin 25a:1:1.english: A minor or a cloth shoe [anpileya] - [An anpileya is] a sock [Old French: calçon] of cloth; [these] are not chalitzah at all, for "man" and "shoe" are written in the [Torah] passage: "And if the man does not wish..." etc.:

Rashi on Gittin 25a:2:1.hebrew: חוץ מן האחרון - דלחומרא אמרינן יש ברירה, ופסולה לכהונה. אבל אינך כולהו, אפי' ריח הגט אין בהם, ולא דמו למגורשת מאישה ולא התירה לכל אדם; דההיא, לההוא מילתא מיהא, לשמו ולשמה נכתב:
Rashi on Gittin 25a:2:1.english: Except [in] the final [case] - For as a stringency we say there is retroactive designation, and [thus] she is disqualified from [marrying into] the priesthood. But all the other [cases] do not even have the scent of a bill of divorce, and they are not comparable to [a woman who is] divorced from her husband yet not permitted to every man; whereas in that [final case], for that matter at least, [the bill of divorce] was written for his sake and for her sake:

Rashi on Gittin 25a:3:1.english: Even the last one does not disqualify [her] - because there is no retroactive clarification:

Rashi on Gittin 25a:4:1.hebrew: לקוחות הן - דאין ברירה, דאיכא למיחש: חלק שנטל זה היה ראוי לאחיו והחליפו, והיינו לקיחה; וחוזר ביובל לתחילתו משום מצות יובל, והדר שקליה כדמעיקרא:
Rashi on Gittin 25a:4:1.english: They are [considered] purchasers - because there is no retroactive clarification [bereirah], for there is [reason] to be concerned [that] the portion this one took was [actually] meant for his brother and they exchanged [portions], and that is a purchase; and it reverts in the Jubilee [Year] to its original state because of the commandment of Jubilee, and then he takes it [again] as before:

Rashi on Gittin 25a:6:1.hebrew: דלחומרא - "מחזירין" חומרא היא, ואי נמי הוה מספקא ליה, אזיל לחומרא; אבל "אינו פוסל" קולא הוא, ואי לאו דפשיטא דאין ברירה, לא אזיל לקולא:
Rashi on Gittin 25a:6:1.english: That [it is] as a stringency - [The ruling that] "they must return [the fields]" is a stringency, and even if he were in doubt, he would rule stringently; however, [the ruling that] "it does not disqualify [her]" is a leniency, and if it were not obvious that there is no retroactive clarification, he would not rule leniently:

Rashi on Gittin 25a:6:2.hebrew: אי נמי כתחילה - כשם שמתחילה היתה בלא חלוקה לאיש אחד, כך יחזור ביובל לאיש אחד, וטעמא לאו משום דאין ברירה הוא:
Rashi on Gittin 25a:6:2.english: Alternatively, as [it was] initially - Just as initially it [the field] was without division, [belonging] to one person, so too it returns in the Jubilee [Year] to one person, and the reason is not because there is no retroactive clarification [bereirah].

Rashi on Gittin 25a:7:1.hebrew: לאיזו שתצא בפתח תחילה - יהא הגט לשמה, ושמותיהם היו שוין:
Rashi on Gittin 25a:7:1.english: For whichever emerges from the entrance first - let the bill of divorce be [written] for her sake, and their names were identical:

Rashi on Gittin 25a:7:2.english: What is [the law] - Is there [retroactive] clarification, or is there no [retroactive] clarification?

Rashi on Gittin 25a:8:1.hebrew: על מי שיעלה מכם - יהא נמנה עליו, ואני מקנה לו חלקו בשעת שחיטה:
Rashi on Gittin 25a:8:1.english: On behalf of whichever of you goes up - [he] shall be registered on it, and I am granting him his portion at the time of slaughter:

Rashi on Gittin 25a:8:2.hebrew: כיון שנכנס ראשון - לאחר שחיטה, ראשו ורובו:
Rashi on Gittin 25a:8:2.english: Once the first enters - after the slaughter, [with] his head and the majority of his [body]:

Rashi on Gittin 25a:8:3.hebrew: זכה בחלקו - דאמרינן יש ברירה, דמשעת שחיטה היה זה ראוי לכך ונשחט פסח זה עליו; "ומזכה את אחיו עמו" — לימנות בחלקו. ולקמיה מוקי לה שפיר:
Rashi on Gittin 25a:8:3.english: He has acquired his portion - for we say [that] there is retroactive clarification [bereirah], as from the time of slaughter this one was fit for it and this Paschal offering was slaughtered on his behalf; and "acquires [the portions of] his brothers with him" [means] to be registered in his portion. And later on, [the Gemara] explains it satisfactorily:

Rashi on Gittin 25a:9:1.hebrew: אמר רבי יוחנן כדי לזרזן במצות - אביהן המנה את כולן עליו משעת שחיטה, והא דקאמר "על מי שיעלה ראשון", לזרזינהו אתא — כלומר, "נראה איזה הוא ראשון" — ולא הודיעם מה בלבו:
Rashi on Gittin 25a:9:1.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: In order to galvanize them in [performing] mitzvot - Their father registered all of them for it [the Paschal offering] at the time of slaughter, and that which he said, "for whoever goes up first," was meant to galvanize them — that is to say, "Let us see who is first" — and he did not inform them of what was in his heart:

Tosafot on Gittin 25a:10:1.hebrew: אי אמרת בשלמא דאמינהו מעיקרא שפיר - תימה, דבנדרים משמע דאיירי בלא אמנינהו, דשה לבית אבות לאו דאורייתא ואין צריך שום מינוי, דקאמר בפ' אין בין המודר (נדרים דף לו.): "ואי אמרת שה לבית אבות דאורייתא, אבישרא קאי ומזכה להון?! ואלא למה אמר להון אבוהון? כדי לזרזן במצות." וי"ל, דסוגיא דהכא איירי אי אמרינן שה לבית אבות דאורייתא:
Tosafot on Gittin 25a:10:1.english: Granted, if you say that he registered them initially, [it is] well - This is perplexing, for in Nedarim it is implied that [the Mishnah] is dealing with [a case where] he did not register them, because [the law of] "a lamb for a father's household" is not biblical and no registration is required, as it says in the chapter [entitled] Ein Bein HaMudar (Nedarim 36a): "And if you say [that] 'a lamb for a father's household' is biblical, he stands over [mere] meat and acquires [it] for them?! Rather, why did their father say [this] to them? In order to make them eager in [performing] commandments." And one can answer that the sugya here is dealing with [the assumption that] we say "a lamb for a father's household" is biblical:

Tosafot on Gittin 25a:12:1.hebrew: והדר מותיב ליה תולה בדעת אחרים - על זה אינה תמיהה, דשפיר מותיב למאי דפשיט ליה:
Tosafot on Gittin 25a:12:1.english: And then he raised an objection to him [from a case where] one makes [it] dependent on the decision of others - Regarding this, there is no astonishment, for [Rav Hoshaya] properly raised an objection against what [Rav Yehuda] resolved for him:

Tosafot on Gittin 25a:15:1.hebrew: הלוקח יין מבין הכותים - ברייתא היא, דבמשנה דפ"ז דדמאי (מ"ד) לא תני אלא מילתא דר"מ לחודה. ואע"ג דר"מ גזר על יינן בפ"ק דחולין (דף ו.), זאת נשנית קודם גזירה. ורבי יוסי ורבי שמעון, אף ע"ג דסבירא להו במנחות בפרק ר' ישמעאל (מנחות דף סו:) דכותים גרי אריות הן — דאמר: תורמין משל עובדי כוכבים על של כותים — מ"מ, כיון שפורשים מע"ז יותר משאר עובדי כוכבים, ומחזיקין בתורה שבכתב, וגם אלהיהם אינם עובדים כמו שהיו עושים בבית ראשון, להכי כשגזרו על יינן של עובדי כוכבים, לא גזרו על של כותים; אע"פ שגזרו על פיתם, על יינם לא גזרו. אי נמי: הכא במטהר יינם:
Tosafot on Gittin 25a:15:1.english: One who purchases wine from among the Samaritans - It is a baraita, for in the Mishnah in the seventh chapter of Demai (Mishnah 4) it only teaches the statement of Rabbi Meir alone. And even though Rabbi Meir decreed against their wine in the first chapter of Chullin (6a), this [baraita] was taught before the decree. And [as for] Rabbi Yose and Rabbi Shimon, even though they hold in Menachot in the chapter [entitled] Rabbi Yishmael (Menachot 66b) that Samaritans are lion-converts — for [the Gemara there] says: "One may separate teruma from [produce] of idolaters on behalf of [produce] of Samaritans" — nevertheless, since they abstain from idolatry more than other idolaters, and hold fast to the Written Torah, and furthermore they do not worship their [pagan] gods as they used to do during the First Temple [era], therefore when they decreed against the wine of idolaters, they did not decree against [the wine] of Samaritans; even though they decreed against their bread, against their wine they did not decree. Alternatively, here [the baraita is speaking] of one who purifies their wine:

Tosafot on Gittin 25a:15:2.hebrew: עשרה מעשר ראשון כו' - לאו דוקא עשרה ותשעה, דכשהסיר שני לוגין לתרומה גדולה, פשו לה מאה נכי תרתי. ויש מפרשים דאין המעשר מתמעט משום תרומה גדולה, כיון דחטה אחת פוטרת את הכרי:
Tosafot on Gittin 25a:15:2.english: Ten [log are] first tithe, etc. - "Ten and nine" is not exact, for when he removed two log for teruma gedola, there remained one hundred minus two [i.e., ninety-eight]. And some explain that the tithe is not diminished on account of teruma gedola, since [by Torah law] a single kernel of wheat exempts the [entire] pile:

Tosafot on Gittin 25a:15:3.hebrew: שני לוגין שאני עתיד להפריש - כותים אפילו תרומה גדולה לא מפרשי; דאף ע"ג דבפרק שלשה שאכלו (ברכות דף מז:) אמר: הני כותאי עשורי מעשרי כראוי, דבמאי דכתיב באורייתא מיזהר זהירי, ה"מ כשעושין לאכול לעצמן, ואפי' מעשר ראשון מפרישין; אבל למכור אין מפרישין כלל, דלא קפדי אלפני עור. אע"ג דאין חשודין על גזל, לא חשיב להו גזל, דהוי ממון שאין לו תובעים, דהא עמי הארץ נמי לא נחשדו על הגזל ונחשדו על המעשר. ועוד, דכל זמן שלא הופרש, אינו דומה להו גזל, שעדיין לא נתחייב ליתן לכהן וללוי. ועוד סומכין כותים אהא דדרשינן בב"מ (דף פח:): "ואכלת" — ולא מוכר:
Tosafot on Gittin 25a:15:3.english: Two log that I will separate in the future - Samaritans do not separate even the great teruma; for even though in the chapter [entitled] Shelosha She'akhlu (Berakhot 47b) [the Gemara] says [that] these Samaritans tithe properly, because they are very careful regarding what is written in the Torah — that applies [only] when they prepare [produce] to eat for themselves, and they even separate first tithe; but [when preparing produce] to sell, they do not separate at all, for they are not scrupulous about [the prohibition of placing a stumbling block] "before the blind." Even though they are not suspected of robbery, it is not considered robbery to them, because it is money that has no [specific] claimants — for amei ha'aretz are likewise not suspected of robbery, yet they are suspected regarding tithes. Furthermore, as long as it has not been separated, it does not seem to them [like] robbery, since one is not yet obligated to give [it] to a priest or to a Levite. Furthermore, Samaritans rely on that which we expound in Bava Metzia (88b): "And you shall eat" — and not one who sells:

Tosafot on Gittin 25a:1:1.hebrew: קטן ואנפיליא פסולות ואין פוסלות - וא"ת: שמואל ובני מערבא במאי פליגי בקטן? הא פלוגתא דר"מ ורבנן בסוף האשה רבה (יבמות דף צו.), דתניא: עשו ביאת בן ט' כמאמר בגדול, ור"מ אומר: עשו חליצת בן ט' כגט בגדול, אבל לרבנן ביאה אין, חליצה לא; ובפרק מצות חליצה (יבמות דף קה:) אמתניתין ד"החולצת מן הקטן חליצתה פסולה", אמר שמואל: זו דברי רבי מאיר, אבל חכמים אומרים: אין חליצת קטן כלום! ואומר ר"י דהכא פליגי בלשון המשנה: דשמואל משמע ליה הלשון "חליצתה פסולה" ופוסלת, ואתיא מתניתין כרבי מאיר — ולא משום דס"ל כר"מ; ובני מערבא משמע להו שפיר "פסולה ואינה פוסלת", ואתיא כרבנן:
Tosafot on Gittin 25a:1:1.english: A minor and a cloth shoe [anpileya] are invalid and do not disqualify - And if you ask: In what do Shmuel and the scholars of the West [Eretz Yisrael] disagree regarding a minor? Behold, [is this not] the dispute between Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis at the end of [the chapter entitled] HaIsha Rabba (Yevamot 96a), where it was taught: [The Sages] treated the cohabitation of a nine-year-old boy as equivalent to a ma'amar [betrothal declaration] by an adult, and Rabbi Meir says: They treated the ḥalitza of a nine-year-old boy as equivalent to a bill of divorce by an adult; whereas according to the Rabbis, cohabitation [is effective], ḥalitza is not. And in the chapter [entitled] Mitzvat Ḥalitza (Yevamot 105b), on the Mishnah, "She who performs ḥalitza with a minor — her ḥalitza is invalid," Shmuel said: This is the view of Rabbi Meir, but the Sages say: The ḥalitza of a minor is nothing! And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that here they disagree about the wording of the Mishnah: for to Shmuel, the wording "her ḥalitza is invalid" implies [that it is invalid] and disqualifies [her], so the Mishnah follows Rabbi Meir — and not because [Shmuel himself] holds like Rabbi Meir; whereas to the scholars of the West, it clearly implies "invalid and does not disqualify," so it follows the Rabbis:

Tosafot on Gittin 25a:6:1.hebrew: ואי אשמעינן שדה משום דלחומרא - ואם תאמר: לקולא נמי שמעינן ליה דאין ברירה בפרק בתרא דבכורות (דף נו:) גבי מעשר בהמה, דקאמר: "אפילו חלקו היורשין תשעה כנגד תשעה, עשרה כנגד עשרה, אין אומרים זהו חלקו המגיעו"? וי"ל, דמ"מ לא שמעינן גט מינה, כדאמר התם: דאי אתמר בהא, בהא קאמר רבי יוחנן, דומיא ד"בנך" — מה בנך ברור לך, אף צאנך ברור לך:
Tosafot on Gittin 25a:6:1.english: And if he had taught us [regarding] a field, [it would be] because [that is] as a stringency - And if you ask: [Regarding] a leniency too, we learn from him that there is no retroactive clarification in the last chapter of Bekhorot (56b) regarding the animal tithe, where [the Gemara] says, "Even if the heirs divided [the flock] nine against nine [or] ten against ten, we do not say this is the portion coming to him"? And one can answer that, nevertheless, we could not learn [the law of] a bill of divorce from it, as [the Gemara] says there: that if it had been stated [only] regarding this [case], in this [case] Rabbi Yoḥanan said [so because it is] comparable to "your son" — just as your son is clear to you, so too your flock must be clear to you:
